meta.title: The E Form: One String Makes It Minor
meta.summary: Five of the E form's six strings are a root or a fifth, so the whole quality of the most-played minor chord on the guitar rests on a single string.

That makes two of the five forms this chapter promised you already own, both now accounted for: the open

from the A form, and this barre from the E form. Both are chords you've likely fretted thousands of times without ever counting which string was doing the work. Now you know: string 2 for the open shape, string 3 for the barre.

That's also why the E form stays the shape you navigate the rest of the neck from. Name a note on string 6 and every other chord tone in the window is placed without counting — two more roots, two fifths, and the single

Slide the whole barre and the shape stops being a fact about A and starts being a fact about whatever root you land on. That portability, more than anything specific to A minor, is why this grip is the one most players reach for first whenever they need a minor chord and an open shape won't get them there.
